title: Pay Order to William Clayton for Stephen Markham and Charles C. Rich, 9 December 1843
handwriting: Handwriting of JS and Wilson Law
source_note: JS as mayor, Pay Order, to William Clayton, for Stephen Markham and Charles C. Rich, Nauvoo, Hancock Co., IL, 9 Dec. 1843; handwriting of JS and Wilson Law; two pages; JS Collection, CHL. Includes endorsement. Single leaf measuring 11¾–11⅞ × 7¾ inches (30 × 20 cm). The left side of the recto is torn, and the bottom edge is unevenly cut, suggesting the leaf was reduced in size from a bifolium or larger leaf. The pay order is inscribed on the recto, and the verso is blank except for a later endorsement. The document was folded in half twice horizontally and fastened with a pin. William Clayton, who served as Nauvoo’s city treasurer from September 1842 until the dissolution of the city government in 1845 endorsed the pay order.1 This document was presumably kept among Nauvoo city records. In 1845 the city of Nauvoo was disincorporated.2 Many if not most of the city records were likely included in the various collections of city records listed in an inventory produced by the Church Historian’s Office (later Church Historical Department) in 1846, when they were packed up along with church records and taken to the Salt Lake Valley.3 The city records are also listed in inventories of church records created in 1855, 1878, and circa 1904.4 By 1973 the document had been included in the JS Collection at the Church Historical Department (now CHL).5 The document’s endorsement, likely inclusion with the city records listed in early church inventories, and later inclusion in the JS Collection suggest continuous institutional custody.
